note: One row per task with a formal result. result: proved | partly proved. covers: fix | finding | note | numbers. Each row is backed by evidence/formal/notes/<task>.md and the Lean/TLA+ files it names.

rows.what: On the published pattern the original checker accepts no answer at all, although the formula is satisfiable. The fixed checker never accepts a wrong answer, and accepts every correct answer written with ground keys.
rows.limit: A fragment with one sort, one one-argument function, let, =, not and and; not define-fun, ite or arithmetic

rows.what: Under the original checksum a run always keeps its first valid submission; under the fixed one it keeps the highest-scoring valid submission. Checked over 5.4 million states, and against the real selection code on 112,944 runs.
rows.limit: Runs of up to four submissions and three score values

rows.what: The fixed flip rule holds exactly when the quadrilateral is strictly convex, and an accepted flip never folds the mesh. On a valid triangulation it forbids no flip the README allows. The original accepts the published folding flip.
rows.limit: One flip at a time; not the whole mesh

rows.what: The original checker counts the true cost minus the last step; the fixed one counts it exactly. The two verdicts differ exactly when the cost lies between the limit and the limit plus the last step.
rows.limit: The per-state sizes are taken as given; that code is identical in both versions

rows.what: The fixed grader never scores an assessment that leaves out a rule, gives exactly the original total for every assessment it accepts, and never gives full marks to a rule whose row records a deduction. The proof found four gaps in the first version of this fix, which was then revised.
rows.limit: Text fields reduced to yes/no; deductive rules only (all 12 here)

rows.what: The fixed grader accepts a file exactly when every test node has one integer class, and then scores it as the original does. Keeping the best submission provably turns variance into expected gain.
rows.limit: Four ASCII control characters behave differently in Python; the size check is not modelled

rows.what: Under the fixed grader a failing or unverified timed call never raises the score, and submissions whose timed calls all verify score exactly as before. The original pays a failed call as if it succeeded.
rows.limit: Real arithmetic rather than IEEE doubles; image quality treated as pass or fail

rows.what: The fixed date test accepts exactly the valid web dates (real calendar date, matching weekday, valid time). Python's weekday rule equals Zeller's congruence, and agrees with Python on all 3,652,059 dates in years 1 to 9999.
rows.limit: The regular expression is modelled by a hand-written parser

rows.what: The fixed check is exactly the 40% test of the risk policy on yuan values, and it can only lower credit. The published position is rejected by the fixed check and accepted by the original.
rows.limit: The exchange-rate lookup by date is not modelled

rows.what: No submission can score above 320 raw; the fixed scale maps the starter to 0 and that maximum to 100. The regraded real submission's 160.76 and 50.08 are exact.
rows.limit: Timing noise is outside the model

rows.what: Two statements the agent must prove are false, refuted inside the task's own image against its own definitions. Both corrected statements are proved.
rows.limit: Covers the two statements, not the rest of the library

rows.what: The original library computes v *= v wrongly; the fixed library is correct whether or not the operands are the same object.
rows.limit: Arithmetic modulo 4 instead of 2¹⁶

rows.what: For axis-aligned rectangles the fixed check rejects exactly the pairs whose interiors meet, beyond its 1e-6 tolerance. Exact overlap areas match every published witness, and all 441 placements of two squares are checked.
rows.limit: General polygons only on the witnesses; rotations and strip bounds not modelled

rows.what: The original correctness check depends only on overall money balance and final order books, so it cannot detect a fee swap or dropped messages.
rows.limit: The fix relies on the project's own tests, which cannot be proved here

rows.what: Each case scores at most 2N², so a perfect submission scores exactly 2543510/121003 on the original scale; the fixed scale and every converted leaderboard value are exact.
rows.limit: The total 92,304 is taken as an input; the 50 case files are not available locally

rows.what: The fixed scale and every converted leaderboard value are exact.
rows.limit: Only the change of scale; the physics convention is not formalizable

rows.what: Every valid answer totals at least 712.538, above the top reference point 395.80, so no score exceeds about 30.3. The promised 5 x 30 s equals the fixed 150 s limit.
rows.limit: A Lean model of the tester, matched to the original on 294 strings

rows.what: 992 game days need about 1,658 to 1,673 seconds per scenario at the measured rates, against a 120-second budget.
rows.limit: Arithmetic only

rows.what: Every published score change is exact, and fully passed or fully failed test groups score the same in both versions.
rows.limit: The identity test itself is not formalized

rows.what: The original body-suppression test can never fail; every published score change is exact.
rows.limit: The report-format test depends on an XML parser

rows.what: A compile failure can never change any score out of 100, whatever else the run contains.
rows.limit: Exact rationals in place of floating point

rows.what: A zero-hit answer is wrong on 37 of the 50 official puzzles, each by a certificate the tester cannot satisfy.
rows.limit: The other 13 large puzzles would need a SAT-scale refutation

rows.what: The misplaced reference point gives a do-nothing solution exactly 2.84005 points, and never adds more.
rows.limit: Per-case scores taken from the saved log

rows.what: Every score lies between 0 and 30, and 30 is reachable.
rows.limit: Simulation not modelled

rows.what: The grader's and the stated excess-return formulas rank strategies identically for any exponent.
rows.limit: The size of the gap (about 0.4 points) rests on numerical sweeps

rows.what: The original test-credit rule can count an unrelated failure as a pass; the corrected rule cannot.
rows.limit: Up to four tests and one or two exempt tests per package
